title: Dört günlük hafta
text: Two years ago a small software company in Izmir tried an experiment. Instead of working five days a week, the staff would work four, but they would receive the same salary. The owner, Kerem, expected that the company would produce less. In fact, after six months the results were better than before. Meetings became shorter because nobody wanted to waste a morning. Employees stopped answering emails during dinner. The number of sick days fell by almost half. However, the change did not suit everybody. Two members of the team said they felt under pressure to finish the same amount of work in less time, and one of them eventually left. Kerem admits that the system works well for his company because the work can be measured easily. He is less sure that a hospital or a school could do the same thing. "We did not become lazy," he says. "We became careful about where our hours go."

questions.q: What did Kerem expect before the experiment?
options: That the company would produce less
questions.note: "The owner expected that the company would produce less."

questions.q: Why did meetings become shorter?
options: Nobody wanted to waste a morning
questions.note: "Meetings became shorter because nobody wanted to waste a morning."

questions.q: What problem did two employees report?
options: Pressure to do the same work in less time
questions.note: "They felt under pressure to finish the same amount of work in less time."

questions.q: Why does Kerem doubt the system would suit a hospital?
options: That kind of work is harder to measure
questions.note: İşin kolayca ölçülebilmesi onun şirketinde işe yaramasının nedeni.

questions.q: What does Kerem's final sentence mean?
options: They used their time more carefully
questions.note: "We became careful about where our hours go."

title: İkinci el mağazası
text: When Meltem opened a second-hand clothes shop in her neighborhood, several friends warned her that nobody would buy used clothes. At the beginning they seemed to be right. For three months she sold almost nothing, and she began to think about closing. Then she changed two things. First, she cleaned and repaired every item before putting it on the shelf, so the clothes no longer looked old. Second, she wrote a small card for each piece: where it came from, and what could be worn with it. Customers started to stay longer and to talk to her. Within a year the shop had regular visitors who came every Saturday. Meltem believes the real product is not the clothing. People come because the shop feels personal, and because they like the idea that something useful is not thrown away.

questions.q: What did her friends think?
questions.note: "Several friends warned her that nobody would buy used clothes."

questions.q: What happened in the first three months?
questions.note: "For three months she sold almost nothing."

questions.q: What was the first change she made?
options: She cleaned and repaired the clothes
questions.note: "She cleaned and repaired every item."

questions.q: What was written on the cards?
questions.note: "Where it came from, and what could be worn with it."

questions.q: What does Meltem think the real product is?
questions.note: İnsanlar mağaza kişisel hissettirdiği için geliyor.

title: Gece vardiyası
text: Sinan has worked at a petrol station at night for four years. He starts at eleven in the evening and finishes at seven in the morning. Most people imagine that a night shift is quiet, and for much of the time it is. Between two and five o'clock he may serve only ten or twelve drivers. But those hours are also strange. Drivers who stop at three in the morning often want to talk, and Sinan has heard hundreds of stories: a man driving to a hospital in another city, a woman leaving her job, a family who had been traveling for eleven hours. The difficult part is not the work itself but the return home. While the rest of the city is beginning its day, Sinan closes the curtains and tries to sleep. He says he has never really got used to it, and he plans to change jobs when his daughter starts school.

questions.q: When does Sinan's shift end?
questions.note: "He starts at eleven in the evening and finishes at seven in the morning."

questions.q: How many drivers may he serve between two and five?
questions.note: "He may serve only ten or twelve drivers."

questions.q: What do late-night drivers often want?
questions.note: "Drivers who stop at three in the morning often want to talk."

questions.q: What does Sinan find most difficult?
questions.note: "The difficult part is not the work itself but the return home."

questions.q: When does he plan to change jobs?
questions.note: "He plans to change jobs when his daughter starts school."

title: Şehirdeki ağaçlar
text: Most people agree that trees make a city more pleasant, but few realize how much practical work they do. On a hot afternoon the temperature under a large tree can be several degrees lower than on the pavement beside it. Trees also hold water when it rains heavily, which reduces the pressure on drains, and their leaves catch dust from traffic. A recent study in three European cities found that streets with trees had fewer complaints about noise, even though the trees did not actually block much sound. The explanation appears to be psychological: people who can see green report that they feel calmer. However, planting trees is not simple. A young tree in a narrow street needs regular water for at least three years, and roots can damage old pipes. Cities that plant trees without planning often lose most of them within a decade.

questions.q: What happens to the temperature under a large tree?
questions.note: "The temperature under a large tree can be several degrees lower."

questions.q: Why do trees help when it rains heavily?
options: They hold water and reduce pressure on drains
questions.note: "Trees also hold water when it rains heavily."

questions.q: What did the study find about noise?
options: Streets with trees had fewer complaints
questions.note: "Streets with trees had fewer complaints about noise."

questions.q: How does the text explain the noise result?
options: Seeing green makes people feel calmer
questions.note: "The explanation appears to be psychological."

questions.q: What problem can roots cause?
questions.note: "Roots can damage old pipes."

title: Yanlış anlaşılan e-posta
text: Gizem sent her colleague Ahmet a short message: "We need to talk about the report." She wrote it quickly between two meetings and thought nothing more about it. Ahmet read the message at nine in the evening. Because it was short and gave no reason, he assumed that something was seriously wrong. He spent most of the night checking his work and preparing an explanation. The next morning he arrived early, pale and nervous, and asked Gizem which part of the report had failed. Gizem was surprised: she had only wanted to move a deadline. Since then their team has agreed on a simple rule. If a message might worry somebody, the writer must add one sentence explaining why. It costs ten seconds and it has saved several evenings.

questions.q: Why did Gizem write a short message?
options: She was in a hurry to leave
questions.note: "She wrote it quickly between two meetings."

questions.q: What did Ahmet think the message meant?
questions.note: "He assumed that something was seriously wrong."

questions.q: What did Ahmet do that night?
options: He slept badly but did nothing
questions.note: "He spent most of the night checking his work."

questions.q: What did Gizem actually want?
questions.note: "She had only wanted to move a deadline."

questions.q: What rule did the team agree on?
questions.note: "The writer must add one sentence explaining why."

title: Dede ve telefon
text: When Yusuf gave his grandfather a smartphone, the family expected a disaster. The old man had never used a computer and often said that the world had become too fast. For the first two weeks he kept the phone in a drawer. Then his granddaughter sent him a photograph of her new kitten, and he wanted to reply. Yusuf spent an afternoon showing him how to write a message. Six months later the grandfather has a group with eleven relatives, sends voice messages every morning and has taught two of his neighbors to do the same. He still refuses to read the news on the screen, because he says the paper version helps him to stop. What surprised the family most was not that he learned quickly, but that he had been waiting for a reason.

questions.q: What did the family expect?
options: That he would sell the phone
questions.note: "The family expected a disaster."

questions.q: Why did the grandfather start to use the phone?
options: He wanted to reply to a photograph
He needed to call a doctor
questions.note: "His granddaughter sent him a photograph ... and he wanted to reply."

questions.q: What does he do every morning now?
questions.note: "Sends voice messages every morning."

questions.q: Why does he still read the news on paper?
options: The paper version helps him to stop
He does not trust the screen
questions.note: "The paper version helps him to stop."

questions.q: What surprised the family most?
options: He had been waiting for a reason
questions.note: Son cümle: asıl şaşırtan, bir sebep bekliyor olmasıydı.

title: Yanlış tren
text: Derya had traveled the same route for three years and could have found her platform with her eyes closed. That morning, however, the station had changed the platform numbers because of repair work. She got on a train that looked exactly like her usual one, sat down and opened her book. Twenty minutes later she realized that the fields outside the window were unfamiliar. She was on the train to Konya instead of Eskisehir. Her first reaction was panic: she had an important meeting at eleven. Then she noticed that the next stop was a town she had never visited. She called her office, explained the situation and moved the meeting to the afternoon. She spent two hours in a small town she would never have chosen, drank tea in a garden and took the next train back. She still says it was the best morning of that month.

questions.q: Why did Derya get on the wrong train?
questions.note: "The station had changed the platform numbers because of repair work."

questions.q: How did she notice the mistake?
questions.note: "The fields outside the window were unfamiliar."

questions.q: What was her first reaction?
questions.note: "Her first reaction was panic."

questions.q: What did she do about the meeting?
options: She gave it to someone else
She moved it to the afternoon
questions.note: "She moved the meeting to the afternoon."

questions.q: How does she feel about that day now?
options: It was the best morning of the month
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Ucuz uçak bileti
text: A ticket that costs twenty euros looks like a gift, but the final price is often three times higher. Low-cost airlines usually sell the seat and nothing else. A bag in the hold costs extra, choosing where you sit costs extra, and printing your ticket at the airport may cost more than the seat itself. The flight may also leave from a smaller airport an hour outside the city, so the bus adds both money and time. None of this is hidden: it is written on the website, usually in small letters at the bottom of the page. The airlines rely on the fact that most passengers compare only the first number they see. Travelers who read carefully and take one small bag can still fly very cheaply. The rest pay for their hurry.

questions.q: What do low-cost airlines usually sell?
questions.note: "Low-cost airlines usually sell the seat and nothing else."

questions.q: What may cost more than the seat itself?
options: Printing the ticket at the airport
questions.note: "Printing your ticket at the airport may cost more than the seat itself."

questions.q: Why can the airport be a problem?
options: It may be an hour outside the city
questions.note: "An hour outside the city, so the bus adds both money and time."

questions.q: Is the extra cost hidden?
options: No, it is on the website in small letters
questions.note: "None of this is hidden: it is written on the website."

questions.q: Who can still fly cheaply?
options: People who read carefully and take one small bag
questions.note: Son iki cümle.

title: Gönüllü öğretmen
text: Every Tuesday evening Nazli teaches English to a group of eight adults in a community center. None of them pays anything, and she receives no money either. Her students are between nineteen and sixty-two years old; some want a better job, one is preparing to visit his son abroad, and one simply enjoys the exercise. The lessons are harder than Nazli expected. In a school the students share the same age and the same starting point, but here one man can read well and cannot speak, while a woman next to him understands everything and writes nothing. Nazli has learned to give different tasks to different people in the same hour. She says she has become a better teacher in that room than in any course she ever attended, because there is nowhere to hide: if a lesson is boring, people simply do not come back next week.

questions.q: How much do the students pay?
questions.note: "None of them pays anything."

questions.q: Why is one man learning English?

questions.q: What makes the class difficult?
options: The students have very different abilities
questions.note: Biri iyi okuyup konuşamıyor, diğeri anlıyor ama yazamıyor.

questions.q: How has Nazli changed her teaching?
options: She gives different tasks in the same hour
questions.note: "Nazli has learned to give different tasks to different people."

questions.q: Why does she say there is nowhere to hide?
options: If a lesson is boring, people do not come back
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Uykusuz sınav haftası
text: Before his final exams Onur decided that sleep was a waste of time. For five nights he studied until four in the morning and got up at eight. At first he felt proud of himself. By Wednesday he noticed that he was reading the same paragraph three times without understanding it. In the exam on Friday he could remember dates and names, but he could not organize them into an answer. He passed, though with a much lower mark than he had expected. Afterwards he read about research on sleep and learned that the brain moves new information into long-term memory during the night. In other words, the hours he had taken from sleep were exactly the hours his memory needed. This year he is trying the opposite method: fewer hours of study, but seven hours of sleep. So far the results are better.

questions.q: How long did Onur sleep during that week?
questions.note: Dörtte yatıp sekizde kalkıyordu.

questions.q: What did he notice by Wednesday?
options: He was reading the same paragraph again and again
questions.note: "He was reading the same paragraph three times without understanding it."

questions.q: What was his problem in the exam?
options: He could not organize what he remembered
questions.note: "He could not organize them into an answer."

questions.q: What does the brain do during sleep?
options: It moves new information into long-term memory
questions.note: "The brain moves new information into long-term memory during the night."

questions.q: What is Onur doing this year?
options: Studying less and sleeping seven hours
questions.note: "Fewer hours of study, but seven hours of sleep."

title: Ucuz kıyafetin bedeli
text: A shirt that costs very little looks like a good deal. The problem is what happens after the third wash. Cheap clothes are made from thin material and the stitching is done quickly, so they lose their shape and the colors fade. A buyer who pays a small amount four times a year has spent more than a buyer who paid a larger amount once. This is not new information, but it is easy to forget in a shop. There is also the question of who made the shirt and for what pay. Some companies now publish where their factories are, which at least makes the question possible to ask. The best advice is old and boring: buy less, buy better, and keep the receipt. It is boring because it works.

questions.q: What happens to cheap clothes after washing?
options: They lose their shape and fade
questions.note: "They lose their shape and the colors fade."

questions.q: What is the writer's point about cost?
options: Buying cheap four times costs more
questions.note: "A buyer who pays a small amount four times a year has spent more."

questions.q: What do some companies now publish?
questions.note: "Some companies now publish where their factories are."

questions.q: What is the writer's advice?
questions.note: "Buy less, buy better, and keep the receipt."

questions.q: Why does the writer call the advice boring?
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Kendi ekmeğini yapmak
titleEn: The Man Who Bakes at Five
text: Rifat is sixty-one and he has made bread every morning for nine years. He starts at five and finishes at half past seven, before most of his street is awake. He is not a baker. He worked in an office for thirty years and he never cooked anything until he retired. The first year the bread was terrible. His wife ate it without complaining, which he says was the reason he continued. Now he gives most of it away. Two neighbors leave a cloth bag on his door handle and collect it later. He has never taken money for a loaf and he becomes uncomfortable when anybody suggests it. When people ask why he does it, he says the honest answer is that he needed a reason to get up.

He had nothing else to do

options: They leave a bag on his door handle
questions.note: "Two neighbors leave a cloth bag on his door handle."

questions.q: What is his honest reason?

He wanted to learn a skill

title: Sınıfta telefon yasağı
text: A school in the north of the country took every phone away at the door for one year and then measured what happened. Test results improved slightly, which is what the headmaster expected. What surprised him was the noise. The corridors between lessons became loud again. Students who had spent every break looking down were now talking, arguing and playing. Several teachers said it felt like a school from twenty years ago. There were costs too. Parents could not reach their children during the day, and some were unhappy about that. A few students said they felt lonely without the group conversations they were used to. The school decided to continue but to allow phones at lunch. The headmaster says the lesson is not that phones are evil; it is that a rule with no exceptions is easier to keep than one with many.

questions.q: What did the headmaster expect?
questions.note: "Test results improved slightly, which is what the headmaster expected."

questions.q: What surprised him?
questions.note: "What surprised him was the noise."

questions.q: What was one cost of the rule?
options: Parents could not reach their children
questions.note: "Parents could not reach their children during the day."

questions.q: What did the school finally decide?
options: Continue but allow phones at lunch
questions.note: "The school decided to continue but to allow phones at lunch."

questions.q: What does the headmaster say the lesson is?
options: A rule with no exceptions is easier to keep

title: Kiraya çıkan ilk ev
text: Ozge moved into her first flat at twenty-three and made every mistake that people make. She signed the contract without reading the part about repairs. She paid for three months in advance because the owner said it would be safer, which it was, for him. She did not take photographs of the walls when she arrived, so when she left there was an argument about marks that were already there. None of these mistakes were expensive on their own, but together they cost her about two months of rent. She now tells younger friends the same four things: read the repair section, never pay more than one month in advance, photograph everything on the first day, and write down the meter readings. She says the advice is dull and nobody follows it until the first time it costs them something.

questions.q: What was the argument about when she left?
questions.note: "There was an argument about marks that were already there."

questions.q: How much did the mistakes cost her?

questions.q: What does she say about her advice?
options: Nobody follows it until it costs them

title: Konuşamayan iyi öğrenci
titleEn: Good at Grammar, Silent in Class
text: Baran was the best student in his English class on paper. He knew the tenses better than the teacher sometimes did, and his written work was almost perfect. In conversation he said almost nothing. When the teacher asked him a direct question he answered in three words and looked down. The teacher first thought he was shy, but Baran explained that the problem was different. He said he could hear the mistakes in his own speech before the words left his mouth, and stopping felt safer than being wrong in front of people. The teacher changed one thing. Instead of asking questions to the whole room, she put students in pairs for five minutes at the start of every lesson. Baran still hated the first week. By the sixth week he was the loudest person in his pair. His writing has not improved at all, and nobody minds.

questions.q: What was Baran good at?
questions.note: "He knew the tenses better than the teacher sometimes did."

questions.q: What did the teacher first think?
questions.note: "The teacher first thought he was shy."

questions.q: What did Baran say the real problem was?
options: He did not know the words
He heard his own mistakes before speaking
questions.note: "He could hear the mistakes in his own speech before the words left his mouth."

questions.q: What did the teacher change?
options: She used pairs instead of whole-class questions
questions.note: "She put students in pairs for five minutes at the start of every lesson."

questions.q: What happened to his writing?
options: It has not improved and nobody minds

title: Kapanan kitapçı
titleEn: The Bookshop That Would Not Close
text: Nevzat's bookshop has been closing for eleven years. He announced it first in a newspaper, then on a sign in the window, then again at his sixtieth birthday. Every time, something stopped him. Once a customer bought two hundred books in a single week. Once a school started sending its students on Friday afternoons. Once his daughter, who lives abroad, sent money without being asked and told him to use it however he wanted. The truth, which he admits when the shop is empty, is that the accounts have never worked. He sells about thirty books a week in a street where the rent rises every year. He also says, without any sense that the two ideas are in conflict, that he has no intention of closing before he is eighty.

questions.note: "Nevzat's bookshop has been closing for eleven years."

questions.q: What did his daughter do?

questions.q: What does he admit when the shop is empty?
questions.note: "The accounts have never worked."

questions.q: How many books does he sell a week?

questions.q: What does he say about the future?

He will sell it to his daughter

title: Gönüllü arama ekibi
text: A search team in the mountains has forty members and none of them is paid. They train two weekends a month in weather that most people would avoid on purpose. In a normal year they are called out eleven or twelve times. Two of those calls end badly, and the team leader says this is the part nobody prepares you for. What surprises new members most is how much of the work is waiting. They sit in a cold room for six hours while somebody with a map decides where to look, and then they walk for four hours and find nothing, and then they go home. The leader tells every new volunteer the same thing on the first day: if you are joining for the rescue, you will leave within a year. If you are joining for the waiting, you will stay.

questions.note: "How much of the work is waiting."

options: They find nothing and go home

questions.q: What does the leader tell new volunteers?
options: Those who join for the rescue leave within a year

title: Otuz yaşında üniversite
text: Hande started university at thirty after eleven years of full-time work. She expected the studying to be the hard part. It was not. The hard part was sitting in a room where everybody else was nineteen and had never had to explain a late payment to anybody. In the first month she felt like a visitor. Then a lecturer asked the class a question about how companies actually make decisions, and Hande realized she was the only person in the room who had watched it happen. She answered, and after that the age difference stopped feeling like a problem. Her marks are good but not the best. She says the useful thing she gained was not the degree but the discovery that eleven years of ordinary work had taught her more than she had ever given herself credit for.

questions.q: What does she say she gained?

title: Apartman toplantısı
text: Eighteen flats, one broken roof, and a meeting that lasted three hours. The repair would cost each flat about two months of rent, and the people on the ground floor pointed out, correctly, that water was not coming into their homes. The people on the top floor pointed out, also correctly, that a roof protects the whole building. For two hours nobody moved. Then a woman from the second floor said something simple: whoever sells first will find that no buyer wants a building with a broken roof, and that includes the ground floor. The room went quiet. The vote passed fifteen to three. The repair took five weeks. Nobody on the ground floor has ever said the woman was right, and everybody knows she was.

questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Sessiz saat
text: A supermarket chain started a quiet hour on Tuesday mornings. Between nine and ten the music is off, the lights are lower, and the machines at the checkout do not beep. It was designed for customers who find noise difficult, and for a while that is who came. Then something else happened. Older shoppers started arriving at five to nine. Parents with small children discovered the shop was easier without the noise. Staff reported that they finished their shifts less tired. The company measured sales and found that the quiet hour sells slightly less per customer but that Tuesday as a whole is now busier. Twelve other branches have copied it. The manager who suggested it says the interesting part is that nobody had ever asked whether the music was helping in the first place.

options: Less per customer but a busier Tuesday

questions.q: What does the manager find interesting?
options: Nobody had asked if the music helped
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Yanlış hatırlanan şarkı
text: Ask a hundred people to sing the most famous line of a song they have known since childhood, and a surprising number will sing the wrong words. This is so common that researchers have a name for it. The reason is simple enough: we hear a song long before we read the words, and the brain fills any gap with whatever makes sense. Once the wrong version is stored it is remarkably hard to remove, because every later hearing is compared against the version already in your head rather than against the record. What is stranger is that people often prefer their own version after they learn the truth. Several singers have said in interviews that audiences correct them when they sing their own lyrics correctly.

questions.q: Why do people learn wrong words?
options: The brain fills gaps with what makes sense
questions.note: "The brain fills any gap with whatever makes sense."

questions.q: Why is the wrong version hard to remove?
options: Later hearings are compared against it
questions.note: "Every later hearing is compared against the version already in your head."

questions.q: What do people often do after learning the truth?
questions.note: "People often prefer their own version after they learn the truth."

questions.q: What have several singers said?
options: They change the words on purpose
Audiences correct them when they sing correctly
questions.note: Son cümle.

questions.q: What is the writer's main point?
options: People do not care about music
questions.note: Parçanın bütünü.

title: İş görüşmesinde yalan
text: Kaan wrote one sentence on his job application that was not quite true. He said he had led a team of five. In fact he had helped a team of five, and the difference had seemed small when he typed it at midnight. He got the interview. In the interview the manager asked him, in a friendly way, how he had handled one difficult disagreement between two of his team members. Kaan had three seconds to decide. He said the truth: that he had not led the team and that he had written the line badly. The manager did not look angry. She asked what he had actually done, listened, and moved on. He got the job. He has never known whether the correction helped him or whether she simply did not care, and he has decided not to find out.

questions.q: What was not quite true?
options: That he had led a team of five
questions.note: "He said he had led a team of five."

title: Bisiklet yolu tartışması
titleEn: The Argument About the Bike Lane
text: When the city announced a bike lane on the main shopping street, the shopkeepers were against it. They said their customers arrived by car and that losing the parking spaces would cost them business. The council built the lane anyway, promising to measure the effect. Two years later the figures showed something the shopkeepers had not expected. Total sales on the street had risen by nine per cent. The reason was not that cyclists spend more on a single visit; they spend less. It was that they come far more often. A survey also found that the shopkeepers had badly overestimated how many customers arrived by car in the first place. Several of them have since asked for the lane to be extended, which the council has agreed to do without mentioning the earlier argument.

questions.q: Why were the shopkeepers against the lane?
options: They thought customers arrived by car
questions.note: "They said their customers arrived by car."

questions.q: What happened to total sales?
options: They fell by nine per cent
They rose by nine per cent
questions.note: "Total sales on the street had risen by nine per cent."

questions.q: Why do cyclists help sales?
questions.note: "They come far more often."

questions.q: What did the survey find?
questions.note: "The shopkeepers had badly overestimated how many customers arrived by car."

questions.q: What have several shopkeepers asked for?
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Uzaktan çalışan tek kişi
text: When her company asked everybody to return to the office, Sena was the only person who stayed at home. Her manager agreed because she lives four hours away and her work is mostly writing. For the first three months it was ideal. Then she noticed that decisions were being made in conversations she was not part of. Nobody was hiding anything; things were simply settled in a corridor and written up afterwards, if at all. She raised it once and was told to speak up more in meetings, which missed the point entirely. Her solution was practical rather than fair: she now calls two colleagues every Monday and asks what they have heard. It works, but she is aware that she is doing extra work to stay level with people who do none.

questions.q: What is she aware of?
options: She does extra work to stay level
questions.note: Son cümle.

title: Kaybolan tarif
text: Nesrin's mother cooked one dish that nobody else in the family could make. She never wrote the recipe down. When anybody asked her she answered in amounts that meant nothing: a little of this, enough of that, until it looks right. After she died the family tried nine times in two years and failed nine times. Then Nesrin's aunt remembered one detail that nobody had thought important. Her mother had always started the dish the night before. That single change made the difference. The family now makes it twice a year, and it is close but not the same. Nesrin has written the recipe down carefully, including the night before, and she says she is fairly sure it is still missing something that nobody will ever find.
